close_reason: Destination reached: turnkey ships one pinned buck2 release; commits 5685c90c..37065860 on top of main (not pushed)
description:
## Destination

buck2 is bundled inside turnkey: each turnkey revision ships exactly one **pinned buck2 release** (binary from toolbox's plain `buck2`, an exactly-named prelude, buck2 source rev + protos hash), resolved from turnkey's own toolbox. Consumers no longer declare buck2 in `toolchain.toml`; they only configure turnkey. This effort carries execution: the map is done when that is true in the tree, docs and templates.

## Notes

- **Execution is in scope** (overrides wayfinder's plan-only default): task tickets make the change.
- Settled while charting (2026-09-25):
  - One pin per turnkey revision, a single record in `nix/buck2/buck2-source.nix`; the multi-release table, `matchingPreludeVersion` and the "unsupported buck2 → caching off" path go away. Prelude pinned exactly in the same record.
  - buck2 resolves from turnkey's own toolbox/teller; a consumer's `registry`/`registryExtensions` cannot move it. Only override: flake-input `follows` on toolbox.
  - Only buck2 is bundled; reindeer is not (nothing in turnkey uses it).
  - `buck2`/`buck2-toolchain` in a `toolchain.toml` is a hard evaluation error pointing at the migration note.
  - Which shells get buck2 is a per-shell setting in `flake.nix`, next to `declarationFiles` (turnkey's own docs shell has none).
  - `buck2` stays on PATH. A read-only `turnkey.buck2.version` surfaces the pin (welcome message, docs).
  - Built on main, which since 2026-09-25 carries the test-result-caching stack (turnkey-vnm) and the toolbox update to buck2 2026-09-15 (turnkey-q7r); the remaining work of turnkey-q7r (upgrade checklist) folds into this map, rewritten as "how to bump turnkey's buck2 pin".
  - The test-runner parity suite gates every pin bump (CI gate if fast enough).
- Record as an ADR ("turnkey owns the buck2 version") + CONTEXT.md term **Pinned buck2 release**.
- VCS is jj; repo-wide rules in CLAUDE.md apply. Consult /domain-modeling for glossary/ADR work, /codebase-design for module-interface tickets.

## Decisions so far

- [Which buck2 and buck2-prelude versions does toolbox expose?](turnkey-luk.1) — both are keyed by release date and default to 2026-09-15, whose prelude matches the release exactly. The pin names a date, never `default`, and records the release's `prelude_hash` as `preludeRev`, checked at eval. Findings: [docs/research/toolbox-buck2-versions.md](../blob/main/docs/research/toolbox-buck2-versions.md) (on main, 827682bc).
- [Is the test-runner parity suite fast and self-contained enough to be a CI gate?](turnkey-luk.2) — it's fast (171 s cold, 6–17 s warm) and needs no FUSE. It can't run in today's CI, which can't build the full dev shell (turnkey-composed can't build on hosted runners, and the disk is too small). A gate would need a slim CI shell with cached cells, Linux only. Findings: [docs/research/parity-suite-ci-gate.md](../blob/main/docs/research/parity-suite-ci-gate.md) (on main, 827682bc).
- [What is the shape of the per-shell buck2 option?](turnkey-luk.4) — `turnkey.toolchains.buck2.shells` (default `["default"]`) chooses which shells get the whole Buck2 integration, under the existing master switch `buck2.enable`. A read-only `buck2.version` is exposed in both modules. The standalone devenv module keeps its interface.
- [Should the parity suite be a CI gate for buck2 pin bumps?](turnkey-luk.8) — no, it's a manual step in the bump checklist. The bump commit carries the parity summary line. The CI gate is split out as its own ticket.
- [Record the ADR and glossary term for turnkey owning the buck2 version](turnkey-luk.3) — ADR 0002 "Turnkey owns the buck2 version" and the CONTEXT.md term **Pinned buck2 release** are written.
- [Collapse buck2-source.nix to a single pinned buck2 release](turnkey-luk.5) — one pinned record now drives the prelude and test runner, resolved from turnkey's own registry with the prelude commit checked. The built derivations are unchanged. The binary on PATH is still left to the next ticket.
- [Replace toolchain.toml buck2 declarations with the per-shell option](turnkey-luk.6) — shells listed in `buck2.shells` now get the pinned buck2 (the same binary as before). Declaring buck2 fails evaluation with a link to the migration note. The pinned binary is passed to the devenv module as an internal option.
- [Update docs, e2e and the migration note for the bundled buck2](turnkey-luk.7) — the user manual has "The buck2 version" section with the migration note, and the examples no longer declare buck2. The e2e tests are updated. brownfield-adoption fails on a separate bug that is already on main.
- [Write the checklist for bumping turnkey's pinned buck2 release](turnkey-luk.9) — the checklist is in the developer manual at `contributing/bumping-buck2.md`. The parity suite now prints the summary line a bump's commit carries, and passes 3/3 on this stack.

## Not yet specified


## Out of scope

- `buck2.prelude.strategy` escape hatches (`bundled`/`path`/`git`): a separate knob (the prelude, not buck2); left as they are.
- reindeer: not bundled; consumers who want it declare it like any other tool.
- Parity suite as a CI gate (slim CI shell, cached cells): a separate effort, [turnkey-kxe](turnkey-kxe), per turnkey-luk.8.
title: Bundle buck2 inside turnkey
